reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read Huldah's phrase in peace as timing, not manner, meaning Josiah was spared from seeing Jerusalem's fall despite dying in battle.

discrepancy.emptyNote: 2 Kings 22:20 has Huldah promise Josiah he will be gathered to his grave in peace, while 2 Kings 23:29 has him killed in battle at Megiddo by Pharaoh Necoh.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Editorial statement of the mechanism; catalogued by Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible ("How did King Josiah die?", contra/josiah_death.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: Therefore, behold, I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, neither shall your eyes see all the evil which I will bring on this place.
sides.verseText: Therefore, behold, I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, neither shall your eyes see all the evil which I will bring on this place. They brought the king word again.

sides.snippet: In his days Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates: and king Josiah went against him; and [Pharaoh Necoh] killed him at Megiddo, when he had seen him.
sides.verseText: In his days Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates: and king Josiah went against him; and [Pharaoh Necoh] killed him at Megiddo, when he had seen him.
